rules.statement: Statements made by a person regarding their own marriage can be relevant under section 32(5) of the Evidence Ordinance even if the marriage took place in a foreign country, provided they relate to a long time past and are incapable of direct proof.
rules.supporting_quote: The provision is an exception to the rule against hearsay and has been enacted primarily to meet a situation where the matter sought to be established involves remote facts of family history, which are incapable of direct proof. In the words of Lord Blackburn in Sturla v. Freccia 1 the ground is cc that they were matters relating to a long time past, and that it was really necessary to relax the strict rules of evidence there for the purpose of doing justice
